note: Expected profile detection for tests/fixtures/nc/okuma (plan M8 §8.4). Owner: WP8.3, G10 fix M8.
One file per folder under tests/fixtures/nc, read by src/lib/core/profiles/detect.test.ts; the margin
over the runner-up is asserted and printed by src/lib/data/profiles/fanucLathe.test.ts, which globs
this folder too, and again with the content score alone by src/lib/data/profiles/okuma.test.ts.
A value is a profile id, or 'fallback' when the content is inconclusive and the current profile
stays, or 'refused' when decodeFile does not open the file at all.
The .MIN, .SUB and .SSB extensions weigh 20 (R1): more than any single ordinary line, less than a
clear Fanuc mill program (f08-tapping.MIN is one, saved as .MIN), so the extension decides only where
the content does not. The $NAME.MIN% header decides under any extension; without a header the syntax
only this control writes does (CALL O, RTS, a LAP call, a G71 thread cycle with H and D or with X/Z
and no P, a G77 tap with K, a line continued with $, and on a machining centre G15/G16 H and G56 H).
G180-G189 weigh 3 only: Fanuc lathes call builder macros by the same numbers. A program with none of
this ties with the Fanuc lathe and goes to it (priority -1 here). SHAFT-OP2, O06-THREAD (no extension,
no header) and detect-okuma.txt carry no extension weight at all, so they are the files that say
whether the content rules alone carry the dialect; O06-THREAD is the tie the thread cycle breaks.
o05-lap-tap.MIN holds the lines the newer rules need.
Programs under a foreign extension, the reviewer's among them, are in _improvements.json.
